title: How to Estimate Your Retirement Medical Expenses Using U.S. Data
description: A deep dive into the Fidelity $315k study and personalizing the number.
content:
The headline is scary: 'A couple needs $315,000 for healthcare.' But averages are misleading. Your personal number depends on your health, your location, your income (IRMAA), and your lifespan. For a healthy couple in a low-cost state, the number might be $150,000. For a sick couple in a high-cost state living to 95, it could be $600,000. This guide breaks down the components of the Fidelity estimate so you can build a personalized healthcare budget.

Key Takeaways

  • The 70/30 Split: Roughly 70% of retirement health costs are fixed premiums (Medicare Part B, D, Medigap). Only ~30% is variable out-of-pocket spend (copays, dental). This makes costs more predictable than people think.
  • IRMAA is the Wildcard: High earners pay a surcharge on Medicare premiums. This can add $5,000+ per year per person to your costs. Managing taxable income minimizes this.
  • Exclusions Matter: The $315k estimate does NOT include Long-Term Care, Dental, or Vision. You need separate line items for these.
  • Inflation Rate: Health costs inflate at ~5-6%, double the general inflation rate. Your portfolio must be aggressive enough to keep up.

Why It Matters (US Context)

Medicare Part B premiums are set by the federal government and change annually. In 2024, the standard premium was ~$175/mo. Projections suggest this will double in 10-12 years.

Rebuilding the Fidelity Number

Let's calculate the annual cost for one person in 2025 dollars.

Fixed Costs (The Insurance)

  • Part B (Doctors): $2,100 / year.
  • Part D (Drugs): $600 / year (avg).
  • Medigap G (Supplement): $1,800 / year (varies by age/state).
  • Subtotal: $4,500 / year.

Variable Costs (The Usage)

  • Deductibles/Copays: $500 / year (Medigap G covers most).
  • Dental/Vision: $1,000 / year.
  • Hearing: $500 / year (amortized).
  • Subtotal: $2,000 / year.

Annual Total: ~$6,500 per person.
Couple: $13,000 per year.
Over 25 Years (with inflation): This compounds to the ~$315k figure.

Optimization Levers

  1. The 'Advantage' Trade: Switching to Medicare Advantage ($0 premium) can save ~$2,000/year in premiums, but exposes you to a $8,000 Out-of-Pocket Max. It is a bet on your health.
  2. HSA Funding: Maxing an HSA for 10 years before retirement creates a tax-free bucket specifically for this $315k liability.
  3. Geographic Pricing: Medigap policies are priced by zip code. Moving from Florida (expensive) to Iowa (cheap) can lower your supplemental premiums by 30%.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does this include nursing homes?

No. That is the biggest misconception. Custodial care is separate. This $315k is just to keep your body running.

What if I'm healthy?

You pay the premiums anyway. Medicare is not pay-per-use; it's insurance. Healthy people subsidize sick people. Your costs will be lower on the 'Variable' side, but the 'Fixed' side is mandatory.

Does the government pay for it?

You pay ~25% of the true cost of Medicare Part B. The government pays 75%. It is heavily subsidized, but still expensive for you.
